## Volatility Forecasts
My work on volatility forecasting. How far can we go by extending a simple exponential smoothing filter?

- [Volatility Forecasts (Part 1 - STES Model)](../posts/volatility-forecasts-1/): Exponential smoothing (ES) is a simple yet widely used approach to volatility forecasting in finance and economics.
- [Volatility Forecasts (Part 2 - XGBSTES Algorithm 1)](../posts/volatility-forecasts-2/): In the previous post, we replicated the Smooth Transition Exponential Smoothing (STES) model from (Taylor 2004) and (Liu, Taylor, Choo 2020).
- [Volatility Forecasts (Part 3 - XGBSTES Algorithm 2)](../posts/volatility-forecasts-3/): We extend STES by replacing its linear component with XGBoost, then dig into why RMSE can underperform and propose a more stable end-to-end fitting algorithm.
- [Volatility Forecasts (Part 4 — RMSE Benchmarks and QLIKE Training)](../posts/volatility-forecasts-4/): We keep RMSE for benchmark comparability, then refit STES and XGBSTES under QLIKE to see how the training loss changes out-of-sample ranking and calibration.

## Signature Methods
My study notes on the signature method.

- [Signature Methods (Part 1 - Motivation)](../posts/signature-method-1/): I am starting a series on the signature method now that I have some free time on my hands over the 2025 holiday season.
- [Signature Methods (Part 2 - Signature and Augmentation)](../posts/signature-method-2/): Previously I provided some motivations for the use of signatures.
- [Signature Methods (Part 3 - Lead–Lag Augmentation and Practical Limitations to the Signature Method)](../posts/signature-method-3/): Continuing from the previous post, we work through three examples of approximating path functionals using linear functionals of truncated signatures in increasingly less practical way to illustrate…
- [Signature Methods (Part 4 — Rolling Signatures in Volatility Forecasts)](../posts/signature-method-4/): We augment STES and XGBoost-STES volatility models with rolling signature features computed from SPY return paths. After careful feature selection, regularization tuning, and multi-channel augmentation, we conclude that the results are negative but instructive.

## Short Rate Models
A long-running refresher series on short-rate and term-structure models.

- [Short Rate Models (Part 1: Introducing Merton's Model)](../posts/short-rate-models-1/): Welcome to my refresher series on short-rate models, dear reader! These mathematical marvels are not just academic curiosities but crucial tools in finance.
- [Short Rate Models (Part 2: Simulating and Calibrating the Merton Model)](../posts/short-rate-models-2/): Let us continue our refresher series on short-rate models. We introduced the Merton short rate model in the previous post.
- [Short Rate Models (Part 3: Introducing Vasicek Model)](../posts/short-rate-models-3/): We continue our refresher series on the short-rate models. In the previous post, I introduced the Merton model and the Euler-Maruyama method to simulate it.
- [Short Rate Models (Part 4: Simulating and Calibrating the Vasicek Model)](../posts/short-rate-models-4/): In our previous post, we introduced the Vasicek model that used the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process to model the dynamics of the short rates.

## Expected Performance of a Mean-Reversion Trading Strategy
Analytical notes on the expected performance of mean-reversion trading strategies under progressively more realistic assumptions.

- [Expected Performance of a Mean-Reversion Trading Strategy - Part 1](../posts/mean-reversion-strategy-1/): A value strategy posits that the worth of an asset tends to oscillate around a more gradual, underlying trend.
- [Expected Performance of a Mean-Reversion Trading Strategy - Part 2](../posts/mean-reversion-strategy-2/): What happens to the performance of a mean-reversion strategy when the fair value is estimated with a constant bias?
- [Expected Performance of a Mean-Reversion Trading Strategy - Part 3](../posts/mean-reversion-strategy-3/): How does a correlated bias in the fair-value estimate affect the Sharpe ratio of a mean-reversion strategy?
- [Expected Performance of a Mean-Reversion Trading Strategy — Part 4](../posts/mean-reversion-strategy-4/): How does parameter estimation error affect the Sharpe ratio of a mean-reversion strategy?

## Malaria Detection
My capstone project for the Applied Data Science certificate program with MIT Professional Education.

- [Malaria Detection (Part 1: Introduction and Data Preparation)](../posts/malaria-detection-1/): I recently learned more about convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and how they are used to analyze images.
- [Malaria Detection (Part 2: Model Building and Training)](../posts/malaria-detection-2/): In the previous post of this series, we introduced the problem of Malaria detection and prepared and preprocessed our dataset.
- [Malaria Detection (Part 3: Results and Reflections)](../posts/malaria-detection-3/): I was honestly amazed by these results. Even the base model achieved 98% accuracy! However, accuracy isn't everything. Let's break down what these numbers really mean.
- [Malaria Detection (Part 4: Finetuning VGG16 with LoRA)](../posts/malaria-detection-4/): In the previous post, we built a finetuned VGG16-based model (Model 4) to detect malaria from cell images.
